Report_ID: Biochemically confirmed (ECO<10 ppm) 7-day point-prevalence cigarette abstinence at 6 months, intention-to-treat
Title: A randomized trial of a web-based tobacco treatment and online community support for people with HIV attempting to quit smoking cigarettes
Author: Jonathan Shuter et al.
Comment: This is the behavioural support + NRT subgroup because both randomized arms were offered the same 12-week nicotine-patch course. Eight participants reporting abstinence during COVID-19 restrictions lacked contemporaneous biochemical verification and were accepted by self-report; four were later recalled and all four had ECO levels in the abstinent range. The direct primary-outcome text reports OR 1.82 (95% CI 1.04–3.18), P=.03; Table 2 gives slightly different bivariable values, so the primary-outcome result was used.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Positively Smoke Free on the Web (PSFW+) plus an offer of 12 weeks of nicotine patches') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: Two urban HIV care sites in New York City and Baltimore
Medium: Mobile-optimized interactive web intervention with online community support
Content length: Eight lessons intended for delivery over 42 days and eight 5–10 minute video sessions
interaction_type: Interactive web content, text/email reminders, and human-human online community support
Participant type: Adults with laboratory-confirmed HIV infection who currently smoked cigarettes and were motivated to quit
Recruitment source: Provider referral, direct contact in clinic waiting areas, and self-referral from locally distributed flyers at two HIV clinical sites
Outcome measurement: Self-reported 7-day cigarette abstinence with biochemical verification by exhaled carbon monoxide <10 ppm; intention-to-treat, with participants lost to follow-up assumed non-abstinent
Outcome variable: Biochemically confirmed (ECO<10 ppm) 7-day point-prevalence cigarette abstinence at 6 months, intention-to-treat

Title: Efficacy of Cell Phone–Delivered Smoking Cessation Counseling for Persons Living With HIV/AIDS: 3-Month Outcomes

Comment: The odds ratio is age-adjusted. Report_ID: Self-reported continuous abstinence biochemically verified by a CO breath test at 6 months
Title: Smartphone App and Carbon Monoxide Self-Monitoring Support for Smoking Cessation: A Randomized Controlled Trial Nested into the Swiss HIV Cohort Study
Author: Dmitry Gryaznov et al.
Comment: Nicotine replacement therapy was available at physician discretion in both arms rather than being randomized as a fixed matched component; 24/42 intervention and 18/39 control participants received it. Accordingly, this is best treated as behavioural support added to usual care with optional NRT in both arms, not as a clean randomized behavioural-support-plus-NRT comparison. The trial was terminated early and described as underpowered. Three participants were lost to follow-up, but the stated primary intention-to-treat method counted missing smoking-status data as smoking.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('CO self-monitoring with mobile phone-based feedback and Stop-tabac.ch app-based smoking-cessation support plus usual care') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Pragmatic two-arm parallel randomized controlled trial nested in the Swiss HIV Cohort Study
Study Environment: Swiss HIV Cohort Study centers during routine biannual cohort visits
Medium: Stop-tabac.ch smartphone app, mobile-phone feedback, text reminders, and personal iCO Smokerlyzer
Topic of Content: Behavioural smoking-cessation support and carbon-monoxide self-monitoring
interaction_type: App-based coaching and feedback plus clinician counselling
Participant type: HIV-positive people smoking at least 3 cigarettes per day
Outcome measurement: Self-reported continuous abstinence, defined as no more than 5 cigarettes since the start of the abstinence period, verified at 6 months by an in-person exhaled CO breath test with a 7 ppm cutoff; missing data or a positive CO test counted as smoking
Outcome variable: Self-reported continuous abstinence biochemically verified by a CO breath test at 6 months
